name: Finance
navDesc: How the design that makes games worth opening can make a finance app worth opening too.

hero.kicker: The Mechanics Playbook, for finance apps
hero.headline: Stop designing engagement from a blank page.
hero.sub: Most product teams guess. The Mechanics Playbook is a library of engagement mechanics documented from real apps across categories, so your team builds on what has already shipped: what it looks like, how it works, and the conditions that decide whether it would work in your app.

logoStrip.label: Some of the apps documented in the library

problems.intro: Users drop after onboarding and the retention curve flattens no matter what ships. Every engagement feature starts from scratch, and somewhere out there six apps have already solved the same problem in public, you just have no fast way to see how. And the fixes on offer feel wrong: you want users to return because the app became part of their routine, not because they were tricked into it.
problems.title: The behavior problems every finance app carries

items.title: Top of wallet
items.lead: Your card competes with two others at every checkout.
items.body: The question is never whether the card is good. It is whether it is the one a customer reaches for without thinking. The apps that win that reach give people a small, renewing reason to open the app between purchases.

items.title: Savings behaviour
items.lead: Customers want to save and mostly don't.
items.body: The gap between wanting to save and saving is old and stubborn. The apps that narrow it break a distant goal into steps small enough to feel doable and make each step visible.

items.title: Financial literacy
items.lead: Education that feels like homework gets ignored.
items.body: People rarely set aside time to learn about money, so the lesson has to arrive inside the activity, one idea at the moment it is useful. Several apps outside finance have solved exactly this.

items.title: The salary account
items.lead: Customers change jobs more often than they change banks.
items.body: The account a customer never bothers to leave is one they have quietly invested in: history, progress, a standing they would lose by walking away. Finance apps rarely build that on purpose. Games always do.

items.title: Cashback that sticks
items.lead: Flat rewards get noticed once and forgotten.
items.body: A reward changes behaviour only while a customer can feel it. The apps that keep it felt make it visible and slightly earned: a streak worth continuing, a milestone in sight.

items.title: Onboarding and activation
items.lead: The first session decides who stays past day one.
items.body: A new user needs one clear thing to do and one small win for doing it. The opening minutes are where people quietly decide whether to return.

guide.body: We have sat with the blank page too. "What have other apps done here" is the question every product team asks and nobody can answer quickly. So we made answering it our whole job. The Mechanics Playbook documents engagement mechanics from real apps: what shipped, in which products, how each piece is built, and how the pieces fit together into systems. Not a theory of what works. A record of what exists, organized so your team can find what fits.
guide.crossCategoryBody: Your users' sense of what an app should feel like is set by Duolingo, Strava, and Candy Crush, not by other banks. That is why the library covers every category. The standard is set outside finance; what fits your product is the question the breakdowns answer.

reportCapture.body: See how finance apps use game design today. Enter your email and the finance report opens instantly, and the newest breakdowns arrive every week. A look at what your team would be working with.

weeklyDigest.title: Three new breakdowns in your inbox, every week
weeklyDigest.body: One mechanic from each app we break down, what it does, and the takeaway your team can use. The fastest way to see how The Mechanics Playbook works before giving your team full access.
